messages:
Jordan: Hey team — getting a SIG/CAIQ from a prospect (ZenLeaf). They sent the questionnaire + a short checklist, deadline next Wed. Can someone pick this up? <https://files.redwood.com/zenleaf/sig_zenleaf_v1.zip|SIG attached>

Jordan: Quick clarification they asked: "Are embeddings stored outside the request lifecycle (e.g., in our analytics DB)?" — Sales needs an approved answer to put in the questionnaire.

Maya: Assigned — I can triage. @security-requests-bot please create a ticket and tag for privacy/legal.

security-requests-bot: Ticket created: RINF-2026-442. Priority: P2. Assignees: Maya. Due: 2026-03-25.

Maya: Jordan — do we know if this customer will use Hosted or Dedicated for the POC? That changes the canonical answer about storage/residency.

Jordan: POC will start on Hosted initially (they want fast eval) but may move to Dedicated if we land the deal. They specifically call out "no embeddings stored in our analytics" as a compliance requirement.

Arjun: For Hosted the standard position is: transient processing only. We do not persist embeddings in user-visible storage; we may log metadata for debugging (token counts, latency) but not content. If they require persistence, recommend Dedicated or Private. I can draft a short answer.

Arjun: Draft suggested text:
```
We process inputs and compute embeddings transiently in-memory for the request lifecycle. We do not persist raw embeddings to analytics or long-term storage for Hosted customers. If deterministic, customer-controlled persistence is required, we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments where storage policies can be configured and audited.
```

Priya: +1 but add a line about legal exceptions: "Unless required by law or a signed agreement (e.g., forensic retention requests), we will not store embeddings." Also call out that SOC/SIG mapping remains standard.

Maya: I'll run the SIG answers and mark the question as "Answered - privacy" with the Draft text + Priya's caveat. ETA: EOD tomorrow for the full SIG response (need to validate a couple of control IDs).

Jordan: Perfect — can you also include a short note about the POC data deletion policy so they have something for their legal team?

Arjun: Suggested POC deletion blurb: "POC datasets will be deleted on request and after 30 days of inactivity unless otherwise agreed in writing."

Priya: Works for me. Maya, please flag any items we need a signed addendum for.

Maya: Will do. Jordan, I'll post the completed SIG answers in this thread & upload the signed template once legal confirms.

Jordan: Thanks everyone — cc @ZenLeaf on follow-up once we have the canned answers. :thumbsup:

security-requests-bot: RINF-2026-442 updated: status=In Progress, due=2026-03-25, watchers=[Jordan, Maya, Priya, Arjun]).
